payout_quote: Washos's own published detailer job ad (via WayUp, quoting the employer ad): 'Starts at $25 per hour and up to $50. Tips and bonuses compliment the quality and the reliability... you will set your hours, receive jobs only in your area and get paid within 24hours... Payments within 24/48 hours of job completion... Keep 100% of your tips and receive bonuses.'
timing: Paid within 24-48 hours of job completion (company's published ad).
eligibility: Eligible to work in the US
Car-wash experience welcome but not mandatory; training offered
steps: Get approved and set your service area and hours
Receive mobile detailing jobs near you
Get paid within 24-48 hours; keep 100% of tips
catches: You must obtain your own detailing supplies and insurance — a real startup cost
Company's ad figures ($25-$50/hr) are employer-published, not an independent verification
Service areas limited (strongest in Los Angeles; expanding)
Physically demanding outdoor work; weather kills your schedule
biggest_catch: You supply the vehicle, the detailing supplies, and the insurance — the hourly rate looks good until you subtract the real cost of running a mobile detailing setup.
upfront_fee: Detailing supplies and insurance required (worker-paid, per the company's own ad).
notes: Source is the company's own published job ad (carried on WayUp), stating $25-$50/hr, 24/48h payouts, and 100% tips. Range $50-$200 per 2-4h job at the ad's rates.

weasel_words.quote: 'Starts at $25 per hour and up to $50' — the top end reflects experienced, high-volume detailers, not day one.

repeatable.cadence: Set your hours, take mobile detailing jobs in your area, finish each car on-site — and get paid within 24–48 hours, repeatable every day demand allows.

maximize: Start with the entry rate to get jobs flowing, then raise your effective rate as ratings stack; cluster bookings in one neighborhood per day to kill windshield time; upsell interior shampoo and wax add-ons on-site since you keep 100% of tips and bonuses reward reliability; market to office parks for repeat fleet/fleet-adjacent customers; track supplies and mileage — both are deductible.
who_pays: Washos pays you within 24–48 hours of each completed job, per the company's own published job ad. You keep 100% of your tips, which come from customers.
who_qualifies: You must be eligible to work in the US, have a reliable vehicle and driver's license, and be able to obtain your own detailing supplies and insurance. A smartphone is required; car-wash experience helps but isn't mandatory — training is offered.
work_available: You set your hours and receive jobs only in your area, but service areas are limited — Washos is strongest in Los Angeles and still expanding — so work depends heavily on where you live.
what_gets_accepted: You get paid for completed detailing jobs, and per the company's own ad, tips and bonuses reward quality and reliability — ratings drive your earnings here. Washos's specific non-payment triggers and removal policy are not publicly stated.
costs_and_unpaid_time: This is the real startup cost: you must obtain your own detailing supplies and insurance at your own expense, plus your vehicle. The advertised $25–$50/hr is gross — subtract supplies, gas, and insurance. Unpaid time: the application process, waiting for jobs in thin markets, and driving between customers.
when_cash_arrives: Within 24–48 hours of completing each job, per the company's published ad.
